body.p:
If you try to push changes and a warning states that your local repository is not up to date with the remote repository, follow these steps:
Pull the changes from the repository using one of the Pull actions.
In the Unstaged files area, select each conflicted file and resolve the conflicts. You can open each conflicted file in the compare editor by double-clicking it or by using the Open contextual menu action. Then choose which changes to keep, discard the changes that you do not need, and save the document. You can also use the Resolve using Mine, Resolve using Theirs, or Mark as resolved actions from the contextual menu of a resource.
If you use the compare editor, after you close it, the file is staged automatically and moved to the Staged files area.

The next steps depend on which Pull action you used:
Pull (merge):
When all conflicts are resolved and no files remain in the Unstaged files area, commit the changes.
Enter a commit message and commit. You now have new changes to push.
Push the changes to the remote repository. You can abort the merge by clicking Abort merge. This reverts the repository to its state before the pull attempt.
Pull (rebase):
When all conflicts are resolved, click Continue rebase.
Push any outgoing changes. You can abort the rebase by clicking Abort rebase. This reverts the repository to its state before the pull request.
